SMTO-MON-0009 — SMTO blocked a monitor command that could delete or change data

GUID: a741d76b-092f-4adf-8882-0d4412d6cc17
Slug: monitor-command-destructive
Domain: MON · Subsystem: mon

What happened

  • The monitor's command looks like one that could delete files, wipe data or shut a computer down. Because a monitor runs its command again and again, SMTO refused it and didn't create the monitor.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the agent to use a command that only reads information, such as df -h for disk space or free -m for memory. Read-only commands are safe to repeat and pass SMTO's safety check.
  2. Remove parts such as rm -rf, shutdown, reboot, delete from or drop database from the monitor command. SMTO blocks any monitor command containing these, even inside a longer command.
  3. If you need a one-time cleanup or restart, ask the agent to do it as a normal task instead of a monitor. A normal task runs the action once instead of repeating it unattended.

What success looks like

  • SMTO accepts the read-only command and the monitor starts.

If it still fails

  • If the command truly only reads data and is still blocked, select Copy error details and send them, with the command, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to disguise a command to get past this check.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A destructive-pattern check in monitor_command_rejection_reason matched the normalized monitor command (for example rm -rf, mkfs, dd if=, shutdown, reboot, kubectl delete, DROP DATABASE, DELETE FROM or a fork bomb).

What this means

  • A configured destructive-pattern check matches the normalized monitor command text. Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.

Why this can happen

  • A configured destructive-pattern check matches the normalized monitor command text.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the matched command form; this heuristic rejection is not evidence that any destructive action executed.

How to fix it

  • Replace the command with a read-only observation suitable for repeated execution. The patterns are _DESTRUCTIVE_PATTERNS in src/agent_runtime/monitors/drafting.py; they are regex heuristics on the lowercased command, so a match anywhere in the text triggers rejection.
  • Use a read-only observation command appropriate for repeated monitoring.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported read-only observation command passes safety validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
